rule: A family is a shared body keyed by genus. Within a family the stat row is shared and each variant changes one trait: a colour, one resist, one damage or shape flag. The 8-colour draconian family shares hit dice 14 and hp_10x 980 and differs by one resist per colour, one damage change (grey) and one wing flag (black). A boss is one body and one stat block with variants that swap the bite element, the resists and the spell list (serpent line, 4 variants, hp_10x 3230 in the file read). Derived undead: a dying creature can leave a copy of its body with a prefix name that replaces the family noun (MF_NAME_ZOMBIE). Population is a depth-banded weighted table of rows {min depth, max depth, weight, shape, monster}; the shape names suggest weight curves but the curve code was not read.

data_fields.name: trait_swap_per_variant
data_fields.unit: trait count (1 resist plus 1 shape or damage)

look_test: A 375-wide strip of our own art: row 1 is eight recoloured mooks of one family with one trait icon each (a resist badge on six, a shape flag on one); row 2 is one boss in four variants at the same size, each with a different element tint and one spell tag. Dom judges whether row 1 reads as one family and row 2 as one boss with four elements. Preview only.
